title: How flying buttresses hold up Gothic cathedrals
examples: What does a flying buttress do?
Why do cathedrals have arches on the outside?

explain.say: Gothic cathedrals have stone ceilings, called vaults, high above the floor. All that stone presses down and also pushes the tops of the walls outward.

explain.say: Builders used rib vaults, which gather the load into a few points instead of spreading it along the whole wall. Between those points the wall carries little, so it can be filled with huge stained-glass windows.

explain.say: At each point, the outward push is caught by a flying buttress: a half-arch leaping from the wall to a heavy stone pier outside. The buttress carries the thrust away in compression.

explain.say: The pier is massive, often topped with a pinnacle whose weight bends the sideways thrust downward into the foundations. Notre-Dame in Paris and Chartres Cathedral both use flying buttresses.

faq.q: What does a flying buttress do?
faq.a: A flying buttress is a half-arch outside a building that pushes back against the outward thrust of a high stone vault, carrying it across to a heavy pier and down to the ground.
asks: Why do cathedrals have arches on the outside?

faq.a: A rib vault is a stone ceiling built on a framework of crossing arches, called ribs. The ribs gather the weight of the vault and send it to a few points on the walls.

faq.q: Why does a vault push walls outward?
faq.a: A vault is a kind of arch, and every arch pushes outward at its ends. High up on tall, thin walls, that push would tip the walls over without something to resist it.
asks: What is thrust in a cathedral?

faq.q: Why are there pinnacles on top of buttresses?
faq.a: A pinnacle adds weight on top of the pier. The extra weight helps turn the sideways push of the buttress downward, keeping the pier stable.
asks: What do the spikes on cathedrals do?

faq.q: How did Gothic cathedrals get such big windows?
faq.a: Because ribs and flying buttresses carried the roof's load to a few strong points, the walls between them did not need to be thick. Builders filled them with tall stained-glass windows.
asks: Why do Gothic churches have so much glass?

facts: Flying buttresses became a defining feature of French Gothic cathedrals in the late 1100s and 1200s, including Notre-Dame de Paris and Chartres.
The weight of a pinnacle on a buttress pier helps redirect the sideways thrust downward into the foundation.

quiz.say: What job does a flying buttress do in a Gothic cathedral?

options.show: Resists the outward push of the vault
options.say: Resists the outward push of the vault

options.show: Holds the stained glass from inside
options.say: Holds the stained glass from inside

quiz.why: It catches the vault's outward thrust high on the wall and carries it across to a heavy pier outside.

wrong.1: Buttresses are outside the building and carry the vault's push, not the glass.
wrong.2: Some carry gutters, but their main job is structural.
